accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS 2.OA.1 (one- and two-step problems within 100, unknowns in all positions, drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown) and NC 2013 Y2 Addition and subtraction (solve problems using concrete objects, pictorial representations and the inverse). Every lab number recomputed: 78 − 45 = 33, 63 − 38 = 25, 52 − 17 = 35 with 35 + 17 = 52, 46 − 18 = 28 then 28 + 25 = 53, Kit's cards 92 − 37 = 55 (sensible), 64 + 29 = 93 not 35, 48 + 39 = 87 (sensible), 81 − 46 = 35 not 127; challenge distractors are the true slip results (123, 43, 101, 35, 69, 45, 28, 89, 6, 17, 88). Parameterised items checked at range corners: p1 a-b 15..74, p2 a-b 11..78, p4 a-b+c 33..74, m1 a-b 21..67, m2 a-b-c 25..77, m7 a+b-c 11..57; all within 100.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented word-problem errors (Carpenter and Moser 1984 problem types; Verschaffel, Greer and De Corte 2000 on keyword strategies; NCETM Y2 ready-to-progress notes): the keyword trap 'more means add' on an unknown-start problem (prediction 3, pickStart 69, CQ keyword), adding the two amounts for 'how many more' (prediction 2, CQ more, m3), subtracting the wrong way round (pickSum 45 − 78, CQ backwards), the smaller-from-larger column slip (63 − 38 = 35, CQ place, m5), stopping after step one (CQ onestep, m9) and treating 'get off' as add (the +18 tile, CQ alladd).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagbarm is a bar-model lab: drag a split along a 78 bar until the known part is 45, drag a marker to the end of a shorter bar so the gap shows the difference, choose the equation whose bar matches an unknown start, drag two signed steps in story order onto a running total, and judge answers by estimating with tens. flagstory acts out one-step stories within 10 with objects; flagcountup and flaginvadd cover missing addends and inverse facts without bars or two steps. Max 6-shingle similarity 3.1% (flag_coin.js).

lab_teaches.evidence: The structure is found by doing: the unknown part only appears once the split sits at 45, so the child sees that whole minus known part is the answer before picking the sum; lining the marker up with Ben's bar reveals the gap as a separate yellow piece; the bar for 52 = ? + 17 sits above the equation cards so the right card visibly matches it; the bus total updates after each step so 28 is seen as a stopping point, not the answer; estimates in the feedback show why 35 and 127 cannot be right.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options disproved on screen: 78 + 45 for 'how many given away' (the bar shows the answer is part of 78), adding 63 + 38 for 'how many more' (the gap is 25), and '52 + 17 because it says more' (the bar shows 52 is already the total and the start is 35).

challenge_feedback.evidence: slip() has nine distinct messages (plus, place, more, keyword, onestep, alladd, backwards, copy, fewer), each naming the wrong step and the fix, e.g. 'Do not add just because you read "more". 52 is the total, so take away the 17.' In-lab wrong answers are specific too: the +18 tile says getting off means fewer, choosing 52 + 17 = ? says it counts the birds twice, and each wrong Kit judgement gives the tens estimate.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes for the family audience: kid FK 0.7, adult FK 7.7. Kid text names whole, part and ? with a worked example for each case; the canvas stories wrap onto two lines at 360 px instead of shrinking.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases; explanation overlap under 12% with Addition and subtraction word problems and Fluent adding and subtracting within 100). Kid paragraphs: bar for the whole; part-whole; compare and unknown; two steps and checking. Adult paragraphs: curriculum and key words; named mistakes; why the bar model helps unknown starts; what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots after Show me on every step at 360 px Android (light and dark) and iPhone 13 (dark). First pass shrank the story text until it clipped and hid the step labels (−18, +25) in dark mode; fixed by wrapping the story onto two lines and drawing step labels in the theme text colour. Bar labels moved to the left edge so the gap label no longer covers 'Ava 63'. Equation cards and step tiles are 48+ px tall; nudge buttons wrap below.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has buttons ('Move the split 10 right', 'Move the marker 1 left', 'Equation unknown + 17 = 52', 'Take away 18', "Kit's answer cannot be right"). say() updates the canvas aria-label and narration after each action, including the current split or marker value. walk.cjs: desktop and iPhone 13 complete all 5 tasks with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors.
